summary: Binary attachment base64 normalization causes idempotency mismatch for function calls between Python and Go SDKs
description: Customer reports that function/tool calls which include small binary attachments (images encoded as base64) are producing duplicate side-effects when requests are retried. The idempotency key validation on the server side appears to treat payloads encoded by the Python SDK differently than the Go SDK, causing retries from one SDK to be considered distinct requests and leading to repeated downstream webhook invocations.
impact: Intermittent duplicate downstream actions (file uploads and webhook triggers) observed for a subset of retries. Affects PineLoop AI's production inference workflows for their document ingestion feature. Estimated 2-3% of retried requests duplicate resulting side-effects.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Using Python SDK v1.12.0, send a function call with a small PNG attached in the 'attachment' argument base64-encoded without newlines. 2) Instrument client to retry with exponential backoff on 5xx. 3) Repeat same workflow using Go SDK v0.9.4 where the SDK base64-encodes with line breaks (MIME-style) before sending. 4) Observe server-side idempotency check and downstream webhook logs. 5) Compare idempotency keys and resulting webhook invocations.
expected_result: Retries with identical logical payloads (same binary content) should map to the same idempotency key and therefore be deduplicated on the server side, leading to at-most-once downstream side-effects.
actual_result: When retries originate from Go SDK (MIME-wrapped base64) the server computes/receives a different idempotency signature than the Python SDK variant. Retries are not deduplicated, resulting in duplicate webhook posts and duplicate uploads in PineLoop's downstream storage.
logs: Customer supplied API gateway request headers and truncated bodies. Example headers: 'Content-Type: application/json' 'X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key: pine-req-20260310-42' Server received bodies (truncated): python-body-attachment: 'iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAA...' go-body-attachment: 'iVBO\r\nRw0KGgoAAAAN...' Gateway trace: request_id=gw-11a2; handler=func-call; idempotency_inbound_signature=sha256:ab12cd... (python) vs sha256:ef34gh... (go). Downstream webhook logs: POST /ingest returned 200; second POST with same logical file arrived 7s later (duplicate).
investigation_notes: - Reproduced locally with sample PNG: Python SDK sends base64 with no line breaks; Go SDK uses encoding/base64.NewEncoder with StdEncoding wrapped to 76-char lines in customer's helper, which inserts CRLF. - Server-side idempotency signature is computed over the serialized request body as received (raw base64 string), not normalized binary content. - Hypothesis: normalization step absent leads to cross-SDK mismatch when encoding variants differ. - Quick proof: normalizing by decoding base64 then re-encoding to a canonical single-line base64 produces identical signatures across SDKs. - Potential attack surface: normalization must be careful for streamed/chunked uploads to avoid memory spikes.
workaround: 1) Customer can canonicalize attachment payload before sending: decode the binary and re-encode to single-line base64 in the client, or strip CR/LF from base64 fields as a temporary measure. 2) Use consistent SDKs across callers or pin to the same SDK version while we investigate.
resolution: Under investigation. Engineering has scoped a server-side normalization patch to compute idempotency keys over decoded binary payloads for recognized attachment fields. A PR to sdk-python tests is open to add canonicalization examples. Proposed rollout: server-side canonicalizer behind feature flag for 2-week canary in us-east, followed by global enable if metrics show dedupe improvement and no memory regressions.
